  "text": "On Wednesday Mara moved the sideboard away from the wall to look for a maker’s mark. Her brother had said there ought to be one, either burned into the back or printed on a paper label. There was only a number in chalk, partly rubbed away.

A man came in carrying a clock wrapped in a supermarket bag. He wanted to know what she would give him for it. When she explained that she would need to see it running, he said it had run perfectly until he brought it out in the wet.

She offered him a tea towel to dry the case. He took it as though she had made an offer for the clock.

Later, the upstairs woman left a cardboard box beside the counter.

‘Things from my sister,’ she said. ‘You can have whatever’s useful.’

Mara meant to open it before closing, but the man returned with the tea towel, carefully folded and still damp. She spread it over a chair and forgot the box."
